judge: pointjudge: two readers, two passes each, one decider
uncovered_described: No code covers a reasoning-field misstatement of the agent's own task objective that does not itself surface as a type-mismatched or meta-evaluative content in the declared query field (the query field here remains a factual, non-meta question, so SP_06/SP_03 do not apply); the mechanism is a self-originated misunderstanding of role/objective stated only in the reasoning trace.

No taxonomy code covers an agent correctly reading and reasoning over entities in the input, then silently omitting those already-identified entities from its own output summary; this is neither a misreading of input (SP_02, since the entities were read correctly) nor a missing structural field (SP_11, since the summary field itself is present).
No taxonomy code covers an agent substituting its assigned objective (produce a query) with a self-invented task (comparatively evaluate two summaries) independent of the resulting query content.

No taxonomy code covers a summary that omits a factual entity the agent itself correctly identified in its own reasoning from the supplied passages; this is neither a misreading of the passages (SP_02, since the fact was read correctly), nor an absent output field (SP_11, since the summary field is present), nor a query-construction or schema fault — it is a content-completeness failure within a produced field.

No taxonomy code covers extraneous unformatted prose preceding an otherwise intact and correctly-formed first field marker; SP_10 requires the markers themselves to be damaged, which is not the case here.

No taxonomy code covers a summarization step that correctly identifies key entities in its own reasoning but omits them from the passed-forward summary, thereby depriving a later retrieval step of the specific entity names needed to target evidence; this is a content-fidelity loss in summarization rather than a misreading (SP_02), an external-knowledge insertion (SP_01), a query-construction fault (SP_05/06/07), or an unlicensed conclusion (SP_15).

No taxonomy code covers loss of a specific, directly relevant retrieved fact from a summary when the agent did not misread or distort it, merely failed to carry it forward for later hops; this is an information-carryover/completeness failure distinct from misreading (SP_02), unlicensed conclusion (SP_15), or uncritical propagation (SP_13).

No taxonomy code addresses a fully parseable JSON object whose declared keys appear in the wrong order relative to the instructions; this is a schema-order deviation without any parsing or type failure.

No taxonomy code covers unrequested conversational preamble that precedes, but does not corrupt or replace, the harness's field markers: the fields are still emitted correctly and are fully recoverable afterward, so this is neither a parse failure (SP_04/SP_10) nor a wrong content-type placed inside a field (SP_03) nor an unrequested wrapper (SP_08).

No taxonomy code covers an agent's own summary dropping entity names explicitly present in its current-turn passages (as opposed to misreading them or ignoring prior-turn context); the mechanism is lossy extraction of currently-supplied facts that impairs downstream query construction.

No taxonomy code covers dropping a correctly-identified entity from a summary that feeds the next retrieval hop: it is not a misreading of the passage (SP_02), not an import of outside facts (SP_01), and not a missing structural field (SP_11) since the summary field itself is present.

No taxonomy code covers an agent's reasoning field misstating its own task role/inputs when the resulting declared output (the query itself) is still of the correct type and content; the taxonomy's query-generation codes (SP_05/06/07) target defects in the query's content, not a self-referential misunderstanding of the task expressed only in the reasoning trace that the agent then recovers from.

No taxonomy code covers a bare arithmetic/interval miscalculation that is neither a misreading of supplied text (SP_02, which requires the distorted fact to be present in the input) nor the introduction of an external fact (SP_01, which covers the import of 1926 itself but not the subsequent miscomputation using it).
